newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE sheds some losses but still ends weak.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE sheds some losses but still ends weak.

text.p: LIFFE robusta coffee futures clawed back from the day's lows in late bargain hunting but prices still finished weak on balance on long liquidation.
The eleventh-hour buying pushed benchmark March to close at $1,500 a tonne mark, up from a low of $1,460 but still down $32 on the day. The contract had earlier spent the day at below $1,500 level.
Analysts said technically, the contract looked sheltered at above nearby support at $1,445, the lows seen earlier this week.
Expiring January ended at $1,475, down $62. Jan/March spread widened to $25 from $3 at Thursday's finish.
The market started lower as expected in a continuation of Thursday's downward reversal to a fresh rally the day before.
Easier New York values in a further retracement to this week's declines on origin and fund sales added to the weak London sentiment.
The day's volume was a light 4,765 lots considering the sharp drop in prices earlier in the day.
With the market see-sawing in the past few weeks, traders said it would be difficult to predict where prices would head next.
Immediately, traders will track latest U.S. CFTC Commitment of Traders Report to provide some trading direction.

London traders also poured cold water on rumours that former USDA crop watcher Leon Yallouz pegged 1997/98 Brazilian crop at 27-28 million bags, which was higher than the 18-20 million bags forecast by Brasilia.
Broker GNI said this contrasted with other strong rumours that Yallouz's figures was actually close to 24 million bags.
That rumours had been out for some weeks now and GNI said it came as a surprise that they should resurface.
Yallouz said last week that he would not publish his final estimate until March. -- Jalil Hamid, London newsroom +44 171 542 4985
